correctness.rationale: An arc between distinct SCCs cannot lie on any directed cycle, so its entire orbit belongs to a full simplex join with a group-fixed barycenter; this gives an actual equivariant contraction. With no cross arcs, open hemispheres x_j-x_i>0 on the zero-sum SCC sphere cover the sphere by strong connectivity, and a set of hemispheres intersects iff its arc set is acyclic. The nonempty strict-inequality cones are convex and invariant under every setwise stabilizer; averaging produces stabilizer-fixed points without collapsing to 0 because inequalities remain strict. This supplies the finite equivariant nerve fixed-intersection condition for genuine fixed-point equivalence. For a general subgroup the signed coordinate constraints determine each balanced projected vertex orbit and the global sum condition. In complete bidirected K_n, reversal acts antipodally on the (n-1)-dimensional zero-sum representation, yielding RP^(n-2), and determinant sgn(sigma)epsilon^(n-1) gives the top orientation. The source includes a 491 directed-graph/symmetry case rational-rank/mod-2 checker; finite checks are corroboration only.

The theorem supplies a computable all-subgroup classification for a natural directed-graph complex and clarifies the boundary between unsigned and reversal symmetries.

final_claim: For finite loopless directed graphs, the complex of acyclic arc subsets is equivariantly contractible when arcs cross distinct strongly connected components; otherwise it is genuinely equivariantly equivalent under graph permutations combined with global reversal to the unit sphere in the signed SCC-zero-sum representation. In the bidirected complete case global reversal yields RP^(n-2), and all subgroup-fixed spheres and orientation characters are explicit.
